hook.en: When a textile mill automates, its cloth becomes cheaper and more even, but a hundred workers worry about their jobs. Is automation good or bad? It depends on how it is done.

objectives.en: State the demerits and limitations of automation
Discuss how firms can manage the effect on workers

narration.en: When a textile mill automates, its cloth becomes cheaper and more even, but a hundred workers worry about their jobs. Is automation good or bad? It depends on how it is done.

body.en: Automation raises productivity and output, and cuts the cost per unit at large volumes. It improves accuracy and uniform quality, works round the clock without fatigue, and removes people from dangerous, dirty or boring tasks. It gives quicker service to customers, better records and data for decisions, and saves time and space. It can make a firm more competitive in domestic and export markets and create new skilled jobs in programming, maintenance and data analysis.

points.en: Higher productivity and lower unit cost
Safety: removes people from hazardous work

title.en: On the board: Merits and demerits

say.en: Put the merits and demerits side by side.

title.en: Demerits and how to manage them

body.en: Automation needs heavy initial investment and skilled maintenance, and it is rigid when products change often. Breakdowns can stop the whole process, and cyber-security risks grow. Its biggest social cost is the displacement of workers doing routine jobs, which can cause unemployment and resistance from employees. It may also reduce the human touch in services. Firms can reduce these problems by introducing automation in stages, consulting employees, retraining and redeploying displaced workers, and keeping back-up systems.

points.en: High initial cost; needs skilled staff
Inflexible and vulnerable to breakdowns and cyber attacks

problem.en: A firm with 200 workers automates 40% of tasks. For every 10 jobs automated it creates 2 new skilled jobs, and lower prices raise sales by 15%, with hiring rising in proportion. Find the final workforce.

steps.en: Final workforce ≈ 156: a net loss of about 44 jobs, though output and skills rise.

answer.en: About 156 workers: a net fall of about 44, so retraining and redeployment matter.

heading.en: Machines for routine, people for judgement

body.en: Automation is strongest on repetitive, rule-based work. Jobs that need judgement, creativity and care for people are hardest to automate, so reskill towards them.
